item.title: Rookie Waldron scores two goals in pro debut, Walleye fall 5-3 to Cincinnati
item.description: Just four days after signing a contract with the Toledo Walleye, 23-year-old forward Johnny Waldron had a pro debut for the ages on Friday night.

item.title: Trump's racist post about Obamas is deleted after backlash despite White House earlier defending it
item.description: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump’s racist social media post featuring former President Barack Obama and his wife, Michelle Obama, as primates in a jungle was deleted Friday after a backlash from both Republicans and Democrats who criticized the video as offensive.

item.title: U.S. and Iran hold indirect talks in Oman with military commander in attendance
item.description: MUSCAT, Oman — Iran and the United States held indirect talks in Oman on Friday, negotiations that appeared to return to the starting point on how to approach discussions over Tehran’s nuclear program. But for the first time, America brought its top military commander in the Middle East to the table.

item.title: Sheriff searching for Savannah Guthrie’s missing mom calls lack of video a disappointing setback
item.description: TUCSON, Ariz. — The sheriff investigating the apparent abduction of “Today” show host Savannah Guthrie’s mother said Friday he was frustrated that a camera at Nancy Guthrie ’s home wasn’t able to capture images of anyone the day she went missing.

item.title: High school basketball: Maumee Valley boys secure TAAC title
item.description: Maumee Valley Country Day boys basketball clinched the Toledo Area Athletic Conference title with a 72-46 home victory over Toledo Christian on Friday.

item.title: Editorial: Noem abused her discretion
item.description: A judge has nicely put her finger on the ugly mindset of the Trump Administration against Haitian immigrants living in this country under “Temporary Protected Status,” or TPS.

item.title: Editorial: Slowed Oregon development
item.description: Data center development in Oregon is six months behind schedule, holding up a $2 billion development that will create lucrative construction jobs and enrich the city and the school system significantly.

item.title: To the editor: Rising electric bills leave Ohio families with few good options
item.description: Ohio families are being squeezed by rising electric bills, and the pressure is coming from forces far beyond their control. Across the Midwest, electricity markets are tightening as demand grows faster than new supply, and households are left paying the difference.

item.title: To the editor: Tale of 2 spiritual gatherings
item.description: On a recent Thursday night, I had the opportunity to attend a community gathering hosted by a local church. At the same time, another event was taking place elsewhere in the city, which while not hosted by a religious organization had religious overtones. While both meetings had faith connections, their purposes could not have been more different.
